scope: Opt-in guarded VP8 RTP/NACK/RTX driver dependency, local macOS arm64 actual encrypted loopback. Instrumented permission fixture; no current Core VideoRepair/Store/canonical host composition or decoded-picture/browser qualification.
implementation: An explicit reviewed interceptor profile advertises guarded video IO without inheritance through arbitrary wrappers. Its local video binding removes native outgoing NACK byte-cache registration before original transmission, while retaining negotiated feedback and incoming NACK generation/RTX restoration. Ordinary registries are unchanged.

Authenticated decrypted NACKs are copied past the terminal consuming interceptor only for this opt-in profile. The driver expands at most32pairs/64unique sequences per feedback item, resolves exact SSRC/sequence and refuses ambiguous senders.

Only successful actual original UDP submission plus a producer-supplied repair deadline creates an entry. Cache limits are512packets,819200accounted packet bytes,1600bytes/packet,256bytes/track ID and4attempts/original. The original producer deadline is capped by the original one-use control (at most200ms). Timer-driven eviction releases idle producers without further media or feedback.

Each explicit repair invokes the retained producer through a new one-use driver control. The callback must reacquire current permission; the cache never submits stored bytes. Freshly supplied full primary header/payload must match the original packet and current physical track; current direction/negotiated primary identity are checked again.

Actual current encoding and apt mapping derive RFC4588 repair PT/SSRC, original sequence prefix and a distinct sender-lifetime RTX sequence. When the answer declines RTX the guarded primary fallback is used. Partial/inconsistent RTX mapping refuses. Pending IO retains immutable original expiry and is destroyed before fixture policy readers release.

The preexisting runtime-close unit test now identifies its Tokio macro crate explicitly, avoiding collision with the local runtime::tokio module. This changes test compilation only. Canonical host video stays uninstalled until its Core/ingress/clock/port/controller adapters are implemented.

verification.socket_loss_fixture: After successful actual SRTP UDP submission, the first seq11 packet is sent to a designated bound loopback discard sink; later explicit SRTCP NACK triggers actual encrypted repair. No interceptor pretends a dropped write succeeded.

behaviors: Negotiated RTX, non-RTX and declined-RTX answers restore exact primary SSRC/PT/sequence/timestamp/marker/payload through the public receiver. Actual encrypted repair headers match the offered FID repair SSRC and apt PT; repeated RTX uses distinct sender sequences.

Current source and target permission withdrawal refuse explicit repair without native bypass. Restored permission plus a new explicit NACK succeeds on the same peer. Cache retains no idle permission reader.

No repair deadline yields no native cached transmission. Idle expiration releases the last retained producer without a NACK and later feedback does not renew it. Four refused attempts exhaust repair even when permission is restored.

Pending socket future holds both current permission readers until original expiry destroys IO; destruction observes both readers still live, then writers unblock. Releasing the old pending gate afterward emits no late packet.

Substituted payload, foreign SSRC/sequence and immediate requested send-direction withdrawal refuse. Full header equality includes marker, SSRC and extensions. Cache packet/byte/accounting/oldest eviction, ambiguity, immutable expiry and attempt bounds pass.
